preconditions.expression: n >= 3 and m >= 3 and k >= 1 and k <= min(n * m, 100000)
preconditions.description: Museum dimensions n and m are at least 3, and k is the number of starting positions (1 ≤ k ≤ min(n·m, 100 000)).

preconditions.expression: all(len(line) == m for line in museum_lines)
preconditions.description: Each of the n lines in the museum description has exactly m characters ('.' or '*').

preconditions.expression: all(line[0] == '*' and line[-1] == '*' for line in museum_lines) and all(museum_lines[0][j] == '*' and museum_lines[-1][j] == '*' for j in range(m))
preconditions.description: All border cells are impassable ('*'), so Igor cannot go outside the museum.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= m for x, y in starting_positions)
preconditions.description: Each starting position (x, y) is within the museum bounds (1 ≤ x ≤ n, 1 ≤ y ≤ m).

preconditions.expression: all(museum_lines[x-1][y-1] == '.' for x, y in starting_positions)
preconditions.description: All starting positions are in empty cells ('.').

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly k integers, one for each starting position.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(num, int) and num >= 0 for num in output)
postconditions.description: Each output number is a non-negative integer representing the maximum number of pictures Igor can see from the corresponding starting position.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == max_pictures_for_position(starting_positions[i][0], starting_positions[i][1], museum_lines) for i in range(k))
postconditions.description: For each starting position (x, y), the output number is the maximum number of pictures Igor can see, where a picture is counted if Igor is adjacent to a wall between an empty cell ('.') and an impassable cell ('*').
